=== DOCS-TRUTH (verified against trino.io/docs/current via WebFetch on 2026-06-08) ===
• DECIMAL max precision = 38 (trino.io/docs/current/language/types.html: "Precision up to 38 digits is supported but performance is best up to 18 digits").
• CHAR(n) blank-pads to length n; VARCHAR(n) does NOT pad — verbatim trino.io: CHAR "Blank-pads to specified length: casting `dog` to `CHAR(7)` adds 4 implicit trailing spaces", VARCHAR has "No automatic padding".
• REAL = 32-bit IEEE 754; DOUBLE = 64-bit IEEE 754.
• BIGINT = 64-bit signed; INTEGER = 32-bit signed.
• CAST overflow raises hard error (NUMERIC_VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE for decimal); try_cast returns NULL on conversion failure.
• LIKE wildcards % (any chars) and _ (single char); ESCAPE clause for literal % / _ (standard SQL inherited).
• starts_with(string, substring) -> boolean — EXISTS in Trino 467 (and 481). VERIFIED.
• ends_with(...) — DOES NOT EXIST in Trino 467 (and 481). VERIFIED — absent from string.html and from functions/list.html. r23:335-360 correctly states this.
• CAST(VARCHAR AS BOOLEAN) accepted values — not exhaustively documented at trino.io/docs/current/functions/conversion.html; the conversion docs only document the cast() / try_cast() / typeof() signatures generically. Trust source-level testing for the exact accepted string set; do not write a definitive list in resources/ without verifying against trino/trino-spi source.
• typeof(x) returns the type name (e.g., `typeof(TIMESTAMP '2020-06-10 15:55:23.383345')` returns `timestamp(6)`). VERIFIED.
• infinity(), nan(), is_nan(), is_finite(), is_infinite() — all exist as Trino math functions per trino.io/docs/current/functions/math.html.
